_doc: Screw drivers as data for the driver_access and assembly checks (mm). The tool path is a cylinder of the tool's swept diameter along the screw axis from the head top outward. head_types: how a screw head is told from its declared head standard (screw_plan / body definition; else the mesh) and which drive it has; tools: drive size per head type and thread (from the head standard), and per drive the tool variants with their swept diameter per drive size, each from a cited standard or catalogue. `use` picks the variant a run measures with (hex_key: precision_driver = round-shank precision driver, l_key = ISO 2936 L-key, swept diameter = its across-corners e max). Per run without editing this file: copy the folder, change `use` (or a diameter) in the copy and run with LAB_CHECKS_DATA=<copy> (child processes inherit it; the result cache is off for such runs). A drive size with no row in the chosen variant is reported as not measured, never guessed. blade_dia_mm (hex_key: up_to_af_2.0 / above_af_2.0) is the precision_driver variant in the shape screwlib.tool_for reads.

path._doc: The path runs from start_offset_mm above the head top to the larger of min_length_mm (straight access behind the head for a driver blade plus fingers, as the mount check's DRIVER_L) and the distance at which the axis leaves the body's bounding box, capped at max_length_mm. max_length_mm 100 = the blade of a long precision driver (Wera 2054 carries 40-60 mm blades, Wiha 267P 40-60 mm; 100 mm = a long-series blade, assumption; the handle behind it is not modelled); was 250 (the body box), which counted parts no driver blade reaches. Parts on another limb than the screw's (the other leg, an arm) are left out of the path: that limb is posed away or not yet attached while the screw is driven.

countersunk.match: head standard ISO 10642, else name matches _CS<digits> or countersunk
countersunk.source: ISO 10642 hex socket countersunk (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

pan_phillips.match: head standard ISO 7045 / 7049 / DIN 7981, else thread family PA* (self-tapping screws for plastic)
pan_phillips.source: ISO 7049 / DIN 7981 pan head cross recess (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

flange_button.match: head standard ISO 7380-2, else name contains NBK
flange_button.source: ISO 7380-2 hex socket flanged button head, M3 to M16 (https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHBtnFlg_M.html)

button.match: head standard ISO 7380-1, else metric thread, head height under 0.7 x thread diameter
button.source: ISO 7380-1 hex socket button head, M3 and up only (no M2 / M2.5: https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7380-1, https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7380/)

socket_cap.match: head standard ISO 4762, else metric thread with head height about the thread diameter
socket_cap.source: ISO 4762 hex socket head cap (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

cheese_hexalobular.source: ISO 14580:2011 hexalobular socket cheese head, M2 to M10 (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/56456/88025f720d57423b9e2c1ceb78304eec/ISO-14580-2011.pdf, Table 1)

low_head_cap.source: DIN 7984 hex socket low head cap, M3 and up (https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_7984, https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/DIN/7984/)

cheese_slotted.source: ISO 1207 slotted cheese head, M1.6 to M10 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/1207/)

hex_key.size_source: socket_cap ISO 4762 M2 1.5 / M2.5 2 / M3 2.5 / M4 3 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/); button ISO 7380-1 M3 2 / M4 2.5 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7380/, the standard has no M2 / M2.5); flange_button ISO 7380-2 M3 2 / M4 2.5 (https://www.westfieldfasteners.co.uk/Standards/ScrewBolt_SHBtnFlg_M.html); countersunk ISO 10642 M3 2 / M4 2.5 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/10642/); low_head_cap DIN 7984 M3 2 / M4 2.5 (https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_7984). A thread a head standard does not cover has no row: such a screw is reported as not measured
hex_key.blade_source: precision_driver variant (Wera 2054: 1.5 / 2.0 -> 3.0 mm, 2.5 / 3.0 -> 4.0 mm); driver_access reads the variant table, not these two keys

precision_driver.what: round-shank precision driver with a hex tip; swept diameter = the shank diameter
precision_driver.source: Wera 2054 Kraftform Micro hex screwdriver, blade diameter / length per size (https://www.wera.de/en/tools/2054-screwdriver-for-hexagon-socket-screws-for-electronic-applications; round blade: https://rapidonline.com/catalogue/product/50-4270)

l_key.what: ISO 2936 hexagon socket screw key (L-key, also the ball-end keys): the hex bar itself enters the path; swept diameter = across corners e max
l_key.source: ISO 2936:2014 Table 1, e max and standard-series l1 / l2 (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/60231/7332b2e7eb6c448b9f8ca6c6ed518206/ISO-2936-2014.pdf)

ball_end.what: a ball-end L-key (ISO 2936 bar, the l_key diameter) drives a hex socket up to max_tilt_deg off the screw axis: driver_access sweeps that cone (tilt_steps_deg x azimuth_steps directions) for every screw whose straight path is obstructed within path.min_length_mm and reports the least obstructed direction
ball_end.source: Bondhus ball-end hex keys: 25 deg angle of entry, sizes 1.5-10 mm (https://docs.rs-online.com/efc1/A700000015447143.pdf; https://www.mcmaster.com/products/ball-end-driver-sets)

phillips.size_source: M2 PH0 / M2.5 PH1 / M3 PH1: ISO 7045 cross-recess numbers (type Z table, https://cdefasteners.com/sites/default/files/product-specs/meti7045pozi.pdf; the H recess of the same numbers is assumed). Thread-forming PA screws have no row (they are no ISO 7045 parts): screwlib.tool_for gives them the drive of the metric thread of the same major diameter under the same head type
phillips.blade_source: Wera 2050 PH screwdriver for electronic applications: PH0 blade 3.0 mm, PH1 4.0 mm (https://www.wera.de/en/tools/2050-ph-screwdriver-for-phillips-screws-for-electronic-applications)

hexalobular.size_source: ISO 14580:2011 Table 1: M2 T6, M2.5 T8, M3 T10, M4 T20 (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/56456/88025f720d57423b9e2c1ceb78304eec/ISO-14580-2011.pdf)
hexalobular.tip_source: ISO 10664:2014 nominal A (point-to-point) per hexalobular size (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/63207/b0c723df4cff4b6290d6d6fd8938e84c/ISO-10664-2014.pdf)
hexalobular.blade_source: Wiha PicoFinish 267P hexalobular precision driver, round blade: T6 / T8 2.5 mm, T10 3.0, T15 3.5, T20 4.0 (https://wiha.com/gb/en/detail/6958f0d4fc4cb5180ea9c16f31391cd1)

slotted.size_source: ISO 1207 slot width n: M2 0.5, M2.5 0.6, M3 0.8, M4 1.2 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/1207/); no slotted driver catalogue data yet: an ISO 1207 screw is reported as not measured
